paper.title_en: Topological states in fractals through a self-similar tensor network encoding
paper.abstract_en: Tensor network methods have been instrumental in addressing exponentially large many-body problems. Most recently, these techniques have also been applied to single-particle tight-binding Hamiltonians, allowing observables to be evaluated on exponentially large lattices. Here, we show that the scale-separated nature of these methods allows for a natural encoding of self-similar structures, such as the Sierpiński gasket, a scale-invariant fractal with Hausdorff dimension $\log 3/\log 2 \approx 1.58$, yielding an exact and compact representation of Hamiltonians on such lattices. Using this encoding, we study a Chern insulator, the flux kagome model, confined to this fractal geometry, and develop methods to investigate its topological states within a tensor network framework. This allows us to reach much higher fractal generations than would otherwise be possible with dense-matrix methods, resolving the density of states of a deep fractal with over 100 million sites. Furthermore, the larger structures allow us to resolve topology in smaller gaps, suggesting that these methods could be instrumental in understanding the interplay between topology and non-integer dimensionality.
